To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. We can select informative and diverse subsets for deep learning with balancing constraints on class labels and decision boundary, and 2. We propose a greedy algorithm with constant approximations that is efficient and scalable to large datasets.

(1) diversity and uncertainty are not sufficient for selecting informative and diverse subsets, (2) balancing constraints are beneficial, and (3) matroid theory provides a natural way to formulate these constraints.

(1) we show that we can select informative subsets that lead to deep neural network models with similar performance, (2) we propose novel matroid constraints for diversity and balancing that outperform competing baselnes, and (3) we show that these constraints can be incorporated into a submodular objective function to obtain an efficient greedy algorithm
